draft.title: Health promotion
card: Health promotion is the process of enabling people to increase control over their health and to improve it. It aims to prevent illness before it starts, not only to treat it.
It uses a mix of actions at once, such as laws and taxes, changes to the environment, education and community programs. One action alone is usually less effective than several working together.
Australia's work on smoking shows this mix. Tobacco taxes raise the price, plain packaging makes packs less appealing, and media campaigns teach people about the harm.
Smoking rates in Australia have fallen over many years. This shows that health promotion can change health outcomes across a whole population, not just for one person.
draft.remember: Health promotion uses a mix of actions to help people gain control over their health and prevent illness.

a.q: Which statement best describes the aim of health promotion?
opts: Helping people gain control over their health and improve it
Treating people with illness once they reach hospital
Making sure each person alone pays for their own health care
Replacing personal choices with rules that apply to everyone
a.why: Health promotion is about enabling people to increase control over their health, which includes preventing illness. Treating people once they are ill is the work of health care services, so it does not describe health promotion.
a.clue: Think about enabling people and preventing illness, not treating it.

b.q: Which Australian action on smoking is an example of health promotion that works by changing how appealing tobacco products look?
opts: Plain packaging on cigarette packs
A tax that raises the price of tobacco
A television campaign about the harm of smoking
Treating lung disease with surgery and medicine
b.why: Plain packaging removes brand design so packs are less appealing. The tax works through price and the campaign works through information. Surgery and medicine treat disease after it occurs, so they are not health promotion.
b.clue: Which action changes the look of the pack, not the price or the message?

a.best: Helping people gain control over their health and improve it
